name: Privileged container
description: A privileged container has every capability and access to the host's devices. Escaping to the node is trivial.
recommendation: Remove securityContext.privileged, or set it to false. Grant only the specific capabilities the container needs.

name: Privilege escalation allowed
description: Without allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, a process can gain more privileges than its parent, for example through setuid binaries.
recommendation: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false on every container.

name: Container may run as root
description: A container running as UID 0 is root inside the container, and much closer to root on the node if it escapes.
recommendation: Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true and a non-zero runAsUser, on the pod or on each container, and use an image that runs as a non-root user.

name: Writable root filesystem
description: A writable root filesystem lets an attacker modify binaries and drop tools inside the container.
recommendation: Set securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and mount an emptyDir for paths the application must write to, such as /tmp.

name: Linux capabilities not dropped
description: Containers start with a default set of Linux capabilities that most applications never use.
recommendation: Set securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] and add back only what the container needs, such as NET_BIND_SERVICE.

name: Dangerous Linux capabilities added
description: Capabilities such as SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN or SYS_PTRACE give control over the host kernel, the network or other processes.
recommendation: Remove these capabilities from securityContext.capabilities.add. If one is truly needed, isolate the workload on dedicated nodes.

name: Missing seccomp profile
description: Without a seccomp profile, a container can make any system call, which widens the kernel attack surface.
recommendation: Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault on the pod.

name: Host network enabled
description: A pod on the host network sees every interface of the node and can reach services bound to localhost on it.
recommendation: Remove hostNetwork: true. Expose the pod through a Service instead.

name: Host PID namespace enabled
description: A pod in the host PID namespace can see, and possibly signal or trace, every process on the node.

name: Host IPC namespace enabled
description: A pod in the host IPC namespace can read and write the shared memory of every process on the node.

name: Image uses the latest tag
description: The latest tag changes over time, so the same manifest can run different code after a restart, and rollbacks are unreliable.
recommendation: Use an explicit version tag, or better, pin the image by digest (image@sha256:...).

name: Image has no tag
description: An image without a tag pulls latest, with the same problems as an explicit latest tag.
recommendation: Add an explicit version tag, or pin the image by digest (image@sha256:...).

name: Service account token automounted
description: An automounted API token lets anyone who compromises the container talk to the Kubernetes API with the ServiceAccount's permissions.
recommendation: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the pod or the ServiceAccount, unless the application calls the Kubernetes API.

name: Workload uses the default ServiceAccount
description: Workloads sharing the default ServiceAccount share its permissions, and any permission granted to it reaches all of them.
recommendation: Create a dedicated ServiceAccount for the workload and set spec.serviceAccountName.

name: Wildcard RBAC permissions
description: A wildcard verb or resource grants every current and future permission in scope, including ones added by new API versions and CRDs.
recommendation: List the exact verbs and resources the subject needs instead of "*".

name: cluster-admin bound to a subject
description: cluster-admin can do anything in the cluster. A compromised subject bound to it compromises the whole cluster.
recommendation: Bind a narrower ClusterRole or a namespaced Role that grants only what the subject needs.

name: Broad sensitive permissions
description: Reading Secrets, executing into Pods, proxying to nodes, minting tokens, impersonating or escalating can each lead to more access than the role appears to grant.
recommendation: Remove the permission, or restrict it with resourceNames to the specific objects needed.

name: Namespace has no NetworkPolicy
description: Without a NetworkPolicy, every Pod in the namespace accepts traffic from every Pod in the cluster.
recommendation: Add a default-deny NetworkPolicy to the namespace and allow the traffic each workload needs. This only has an effect if the CNI plugin enforces NetworkPolicy.
